genxml.title: O2 MACE Fast-Ethernet block: registers, DMA message formats and diagnostic port
genxml.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
genxml.doc: The MACE Fast-Ethernet block: MAC control, interrupt status, transmit and receive DMA control, the transmit ring, the receive cluster FIFO, the PHY bus and the station-address filter. Offsets are from the block base (constant BLOCK_BASE). Diagnostic transmit queue registers, the backoff seed and the incoming message queue have no entry yet.

struct.name: MAC_CONTROL
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: MAC configuration and the MAC core reset. Bits not listed read zero (printed page 70). Reset sets core reset (bit 0) and the read-only revision field to 1, so the reset value is 0x20000001 (printed page 71).

struct.name: INTERRUPT_STATUS
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Interrupt event flags for the Fast-Ethernet interface, with read-only pointer and sequence aliases. Writing one to a flag bit clears it. Writing zero leaves it unchanged (printed page 72). The interface drives CRIME interrupt slot 3 (printed page 179). Bits not listed read zero.

struct.name: DMA_CONTROL
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Transmit and receive DMA control. Bits not listed read zero (printed pages 73 and 74). The table lists no DMA reset bit, although the transmit pointer section refers to one (unknown, printed page 74).

struct.name: INTERRUPT_DELAY
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Receive interrupt delay. The count is in 30.69 microsecond ticks, so the 63 maximum is about 2 ms (printed page 73). A new packet starts the count-down. Expiry delivers the pending receive threshold condition to interrupt status. The count ends early when the receive FIFO drops below four entries (printed pages 73 and 80). Restart-on-each-packet behaviour is not stated (unknown).

struct.name: TX_INTERRUPT_ALIAS
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Write-only alias of the transmit interrupt enable in DMA control (printed page 74). Reads are not described.

struct.name: RX_INTERRUPT_ALIAS
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Write-only alias of the receive interrupt enable and threshold in DMA control (printed page 74). Reads are not described.

struct.name: TX_RING_POINTERS
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Transmit ring read and write pointers. The ring is empty when the two are equal and full when the write pointer is one entry behind the read pointer, so one entry is never used (printed pages 74 and 78). Software writes only the write pointer. The read pointer can be reset to zero only through a DMA reset control whose bit the table does not give (unknown). The page does not say whether the pointer values wrap at the selected ring size, or whether the empty comparison masks higher bits (unknown, printed pages 74 and 78). The second element is an alias (printed page 70).

struct.name: RX_FIFO_POINTERS
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Receive cluster FIFO count and read and write indexes. Hardware updates them atomically. The FIFO holds 16 cluster addresses (printed pages 75 and 80). The text says reset clears the indexes and count (printed page 75). Table 45 also prints a reset of zero for both generation bits, which the text does not mention (printed page 75). Software should not read the FIFO while receive DMA is enabled (printed page 75). The second and third elements are aliases (printed page 70).

struct.name: INTERRUPT_REQUEST
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Write-only diagnostic port. Each write generates one interrupt update packet for the Ethernet tag, carrying bits 31:0 of the write (established, printed page 70). Reads at this offset return the last transmit status vector instead, see TX_STATUS_VECTOR (established, printed page 70). No reset value is given (printed page 70). All registers in the block are accessed as 64-bit programmed I/O (established, printed page 70). Whether the upper 32 bits of a 64-bit write are used, and whether narrower accesses work, is not stated.

struct.name: PHY_DATA
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: PHY serial bus data. A write sets the outgoing value. After a read, the field holds the value read from the PHY (printed page 76).

struct.name: PHY_ADDRESS
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: PHY device and register address for the next access (printed page 76).

struct.name: PHY_READ_START
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Writing any value starts an external PHY read at the addresses in the PHY address register (printed page 76). Reset value is not given (printed page 76).

struct.name: BACKOFF_SEED
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Random-number seed for the linear-feedback shift register that drives the transmit backoff counter. Write-only. Only bits 10 to 0 are defined (printed page 70). Reset value is not given (printed page 70).

struct.name: STATION_ADDRESS
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Physical station address, 48 bits. The receive filter compares the address one byte at a time. Address byte n sits in bits 8n+7 to 8n, and the first byte is the first byte received from the wire. Bit 0 of the first byte is the first bit on the wire (printed page 77). Reset value is not given (printed page 70). The Linux and OpenBSD drivers write the first octet to bits 47 to 40 and the last octet to bits 7 to 0, the reverse of this map (software expectation, inferred; the Linux and OpenBSD station-address load routines). Which mapping the chip applies is unresolved.

struct.name: SECONDARY_STATION_ADDRESS
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: 48-bit secondary station address. The table calls it a secondary physical or multicast address (printed page 70). The filter section describes two physical station addresses (printed page 77). Reset value is not given (printed page 70).

struct.name: MULTICAST_FILTER
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: 64-bit multicast hash mask. A multicast destination address reduces to a six-bit index, the six most significant bits of a 32-bit CRC over the 48-bit address. The packet passes if the mask bit at that index is set. The mask is not an exact address filter, so software must still check the address (printed page 77). Reset value is not given (printed page 70).

struct.name: TX_RING_BASE
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Physical base address of the transmit ring in main memory. Bits 12 to 0 are not defined, so they read zero (printed page 70). Reset value is not given (printed page 70).

struct.name: RX_FIFO_DATA
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Receive cluster FIFO data port. A write pushes a cluster base address, and the low 12 bits are not kept, so they read back as zero (printed page 75). The 32 locations are aliases of one port with no index (printed page 75). Contents are not initialized at reset (printed page 75). Table 46 prints a reset of zero for the address bits, which conflicts with that text. Which one applies is unknown (printed page 75).

struct.name: RX_STATUS_VECTOR
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Receive status vector. It occupies the first doubleword of the first 256-byte bucket of each packet (printed pages 80 and 81).

struct.name: TX_COMMAND
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Transmit command header, the first doubleword of a transmit ring message. Each message starts on a 128-byte boundary (printed page 78). The MAC overwrites this word with the status vector after transmit (printed pages 78 and 79).

struct.name: TX_CONCAT_POINTER
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Transmit concatenation pointer: the physical address and length of a buffer that holds the rest of the packet (printed page 79). The buffer lies inside a 4 KiB aligned area (printed page 78).

struct.name: TX_STATUS_VECTOR
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 70 to 81, 173, 175, 179 and 181)
struct.doc: Transmit status vector. The MAC unit supplies it after each transmit, and it is written over the first doubleword of the transmit message in the ring (established, printed pages 78 and 79). A read of Interrupt Request at offset 0x58 returns it (established, printed page 70). The published layout is below. No reset value is given, and which failures update the vector is not stated (printed pages 70 and 79).
